subject: Post-demo: private network onboarding + embeddings/reranker integration
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martin <sofia.martin@novasec.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novasec.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed integration approach (networking + reranker)

Hi Sofia + Liam —

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation. As promised, here’s a short, actionable recap of the technical approach we discussed and the next steps so your infra team can evaluate. I kept the scope focused on networking + auth (private connectivity), SDK setup, and the embeddings/reranker flow we walked through.

High-level summary
- Goal: Run Redwood inference for chat + reranker calls with private connectivity from NovaSec VPC, maintain low latency for retrieval+rerank, and keep PII inside your network where required.
- Modes proposed: Primary = VPC Endpoint (PrivateLink-style) into Redwood Private; Fallback = regular hosted API with IP allowlist for admin ops.

Technical approach (short)
1) VPC endpoint & private DNS: we’ll provision a private endpoint in your shared services VPC. Private DNS will map api.redwood-inference.internal -> our endpoint IPs so SDK calls resolve locally.
2) mTLS + client certs: mutual TLS for all model calls. Certificate rotation handled via your KMS + our short-lived client certs (we’ll supply CSR template).
3) SDK & auth: use Redwood SDK with mTLS client cert and optional API key (for internal fallbacks). SDK picks best route based on DNS; we’ll provide a config profile for your staging/prod clusters.
4) Egress & routing: allow egress from model-serving subnets to Redwood endpoint CIDR (we’ll provide exact ranges), NAT not required if endpoint peering in same AZ/subnet. If using NAT egress, we recommend SNAT with static IP blocks we whitelist.
5) Structured output & tool calling: tool endpoints (e.g., your document retrieval service) must be reachable from Redwood’s worker tier when using hosted fallback. For private mode tool-calls we recommend deploying a small proxy in your VPC that exposes a limited function-call surface over mTLS.
6) Embeddings & reranker: embeddings run via an SDK call (hosted or private). For minimal data movement, we suggest keeping the vector store in your VPC (self-hosted) and calling our reranker over the private endpoint. We outlined latency SLAs in the call (50–150ms extra for rerank over private link depending on region).

Open questions for your infra team
- Do you want the embedding index to be hosted by you or managed by Redwood inside your VPC?
- What is your preferred cert rotation cadence (30/90 days)?
- Can you provide a list of egress subnets and NAT IPs for allowlisting?

Next steps (owners + timeline)
- Redwood to share integration checklist + sample SDK profile (PR: Priya) — by Mon 2026-06-01. (attached: redwood_integration_checklist.csv)
- NovaSec infra to confirm VPC endpoint support and share subnet/CIDR details (owner: Sofia) — target Tue 2026-06-02.
- Dev to draft mTLS CSR template and cert rotation notes (owner: Dev) — Wed 2026-06-03.
- Engineering sync if needed: 30–40 min deep-dive next week.

Attachments: redwood_integration_checklist.csv, novasec_vpc_diagram.png

Thanks — I’ll pause here and pick up once I have your infra notes.

— Priya

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed integration approach (networking + reranker)

Priya —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers from infra:
- We can provision a PrivateLink endpoint; will confirm exact subnet ranges tomorrow.
- We prefer 90-day cert rotation and we use HashiCorp Vault for issuing client certs. We can accept a CSR.
- We will host the embedding index in our VPC (managed by us) for now; want Redwood to call the reranker over the private endpoint.

Two clarifying questions from our security team:
1) For mTLS, does Redwood accept Vault-issued client certs, or do you require Redwood-managed certs for client identity?
2) If we keep embeddings in our VPC, will we need to expose any ports to Redwood workers, or is all traffic initiated from your side to ours?

We can do the engineering sync on Tue 2026-06-02 at 10:00 PT if that works.

Thanks,
Sofia

sofia.martin@novasec.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sofia Martin <sofia.martin@novasec.com>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed integration approach (networking + reranker)

Thanks — quick technical notes to prepare for the sync and to answer Sofia’s security questions: 

1) Vault-issued certs: we support customer-issued client certs (Vault) as long as the cert chains to a CA we trust. Workflow we recommend: you create a root/intermediate in Vault -> sign client cert CSR we provide -> rotate by issuing new certs through Vault and updating CSR template. We can provide an automated cert rotation script to call Vault’s API.

2) Embeddings location & connection model: since NovaSec will host the vector store, we expect Redwood reranker to connect to a small secure RPC endpoint you run in your VPC. Two supported connection models:
  a) Inbound from Redwood workers to your RPC over the private endpoint (recommended). Network requirements: allow inbound from Redwood endpoint CIDR to your RPC port (we prefer TLS on 8443).
  b) Reverse-proxy/pull model: deploy a proxy that periodically pulls batches for rerank — more work on your side but avoids opening inbound ports.

3) Networking specifics we’ll send in the checklist:
  - Exact Redwood endpoint CIDR block for allowlist (we will publish a /24 per region).
  - Health check traffic uses ports 443/8443 to the RPC address; ensure route table entries from our AZs to your subnets.
  - Private DNS TTL is low (60s) to support failover to hosted API when private endpoint is down. SDK fallbacks: SDK will prefer private endpoint, then hosted API if explicit fallback enabled.

4) Tool-calling & structured output: tool-calls that contain sensitive payloads should be proxied through your in-VPC proxy. For non-sensitive tool calls (e.g., public search), we can use hosted tool endpoints.

I’ll prepare a short doc with the CSR template and exact CIDR + port list before the Tue sync.

— Dev
